questions.q: Which of these is a direct identifier rather than a quasi-identifier?
options: A 5-digit ZIP code
A full date of birth
A Social Security number
A gender field
questions.explain: A Social Security number identifies a specific person on its own. ZIP code, birth date, and gender are quasi-identifiers — each is shared by many people, but together they can narrow a dataset down to one person.

questions.q: What makes quasi-identifiers like ZIP code, birth date, and gender dangerous, according to this lesson?
options: They are illegal to collect in most countries
Each one alone identifies a person, just like a name does
Combined, a small number of them can uniquely re-identify most people, even with names and SSNs removed
They are always encrypted by default, giving a false sense of security
questions.explain: No single quasi-identifier points to one person, but Latanya Sweeney's research showed that combining just a few of them re-identifies a large majority of the population, even after direct identifiers are stripped out.

questions.q: Per Latanya Sweeney's 2000 Carnegie Mellon research, which three fields in combination uniquely identify a large majority of the U.S. population?
options: Name, email address, and phone number
5-digit ZIP code, full date of birth, and gender
Credit card number, bank name, and account number
IP address, device ID, and browser type
questions.explain: Sweeney's 'Simple Demographics Often Identify People Uniquely' found that 5-digit ZIP code, full birth date, and gender together uniquely identify a large majority of the U.S. population — the classic example of quasi-identifier re-identification.

questions.q: How does GDPR's concept of 'personal data' compare to the US-centric term PII?
options: They mean exactly the same thing and are fully interchangeable
Personal data is narrower — it excludes anything not directly naming a person
Personal data is broader — it covers any information relating to an identified or identifiable person, including things like IP addresses and cookie IDs
PII is a European legal term and personal data is an American one
questions.explain: GDPR defines personal data broadly as any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, which catches data like IP addresses, device IDs, and location history that a narrower PII framing might miss.

questions.q: What does this lesson preview as 'special category' or sensitive PII, to be covered fully in Lesson 3?
options: Any data stored in a cloud database
Marketing preference data like favorite product categories
Health information, biometric data, and detailed financial account data
Publicly posted social media usernames
questions.explain: Health records, biometric identifiers, and financial account data are singled out because exposure can cause direct, serious harm to the person — GDPR calls this special category data, and Lesson 3 covers it alongside organizational confidential data.
